Wayfare is Meridian Studio's realtime departure-display program for Halcyon
Transit: platform displays for three pilot stations — Ashport Central, Ferry
Quay, Millbrook Bridge — fed by live vehicle-position data.

Scope agreed at the kickoff (2026-02-20) with Petra Lindqvist: sub-second
perceived freshness, outdoor readability, and a June ship date. The displays
speak MQTT (decision d-002) and went from per-display autonomy (d-003) to an
edge-gateway hub (d-008) after field maintenance pain. The palette is
green-and-amber for outdoor readability (d-009).

Team: Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer), June Park (design),
Bram Oyelaran (fleet), Katrin Ilic (QA), Theo Kanda (systems).
Shipped 2026-06-12; ship retro in m-008.

final_answer:
Based on my examination of the session files, the earliest Wayfare-related session is **s-002 "Wayfare display firmware first light"** dated **2026-03-05**.

**What it achieved:**
- First firmware boot on the bench with a single-board computer rendering the departure board
- Successfully pulled MQTT retained messages per decision d-002
- Local fallback rendering works — power-cycling the board restores the last-known board in under two seconds

**Evidence:**

From `/tmp/kal-corpus-Fa0XXU/corpus/sessions/s-002.md`:
```

First firmware boot on the bench: one single-board computer rendering the
departure board, pulling MQTT retained messages per d-002. Local fallback
rendering works — power-cycle the board and it paints the last-known board in
under two seconds.
```

I verified this is the earliest Wayfare session by checking sessions s-001 through s-010 chronologically (s-001 is 2026-02-19 but is about Ledgerline, not Wayfare). The Wayfare project itself was created on 2026-02-26 (per `/tmp/kal-corpus-Fa0XXU/corpus/projects/wayfare.md`), making s-002 from 2026-03-05 the first documented Wayfare session.
